comment: LED / flashlight / notification-LED policy for the S10+ (beyond2lte). Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-led-diag.sh. Which LED classes the hardware actually exposes is ENUMERATED at runtime and reported truthfully: a class that is absent is NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE, never silently emulated. There is an explicit OFF state and nothing is switched on at boot.

known_hardware.rear_flash: dual-LED flash (warm/cool) driven by the camera/PMIC LED class
known_hardware.front_notification: S10+ carries a front notification LED; whether a Linux LED class is bound is reported, not assumed
known_hardware.display: S6E3HA9 AMOLED, curved edges; edge lighting is a SOFTWARE display effect, not a separate LED

flashlight.comment: Torch/white flash. Candidates are probed in order; the FIRST that responds wins and its real path is reported.

notification.comment: Front notification LED. A notification LED that does not exist on this kernel is NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE; the notifier then falls back to the display (a different, honest path).

edge_lighting.comment: TRUTHFUL: the S10+ has no dedicated edge-lighting LED. Samsung's 'Edge lighting' is a display overlay on the curved AMOLED driven by the display bridge, so this repository models it as a display effect and reports hardware_led=false. It therefore depends on the display bridge (nuxel-wl-fb) and is NOT_VERIFIED.
edge_lighting.fallback: use the notification LED class if present, else a display overlay when the display bridge is up

safety.comment: Thermal and battery guard for the torch: the torch is a real 1 W-class emitter, so a bounded ON time and an explicit OFF are mandatory, and nothing turns it on automatically.
